metaData.originalTitle: Gemini 3.5 Flash: more expensive， but Google plan to use it for everything
metaData.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash: more expensive， but Google plan to use it for everything
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Google released Gemini 3.5 Flash at I/O 2026 with a significant price increase, rolling it out across key products like Search and the Gemini app, while introducing a new Interactions API.
metaData.summary: Simon Willison reports on the release of Gemini 3.5 Flash at Google I/O 2026, noting it skipped the preview phase and went straight to general availability. Google is integrating the model into its key products, including the Gemini app, AI Mode in Google Search, and developer platforms like Google Antigravity and Android Studio. The model supports 1,048,576 input tokens and 65,536 output tokens, with a knowledge cut-off of January 2025. A notable change is the price increase: 3.5 Flash is 3x the cost of 3 Flash Preview and 6x the cost of 3.1 Flash-Lite, at $1.50/million input and $9/million output. This aligns with a broader industry trend of rising API prices from OpenAI and Anthropic. Willison also tests the model's image generation capabilities with an SVG prompt, producing a stylized pelican on a bicycle at a cost of roughly 13 cents. The article provides a concise, data-driven analysis of the model's specs, pricing, and deployment strategy.

mainPoints.point: Gemini 3.5 Flash is released directly to general availability and integrated into Google's core products.
mainPoints.explanation: The model is available in the Gemini app, Google Search AI Mode, and developer platforms, signaling Google's confidence in its readiness for widespread use.

mainPoints.point: The model comes with a significant price increase, reflecting a broader industry trend.
mainPoints.explanation: At $1.50/million input and $9/million output, it is 3x the price of its predecessor, aligning with similar price hikes from OpenAI and Anthropic for their latest models.

mainPoints.point: Google introduces a new Interactions API for server-side history management.
mainPoints.explanation: This API, currently in beta, mirrors patterns from OpenAI's Responses API, enabling developers to manage conversation history on the server side.

keyQuotes: 3.5 Flash is available today to billions of people globally.
Given the price increase it's interesting to see Google roll it out for so many of their own free-to-consumer products.
It feels like all three of the major AI labs are starting to probe the price tolerance of their API customers.
